issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String parameter (the saloon name), but the solution implements a no-argument constructor and the provided Main uses a no-arg instantiation. This mismatch between the specification and the concrete code will confuse students about the required constructor signature and the expected internal fields (e.g., a name field and its getter).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the solution and template Main to implement/use SealSaloon(String name) (add a private name field and a getter) so it matches the problem statement and UML; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to specify a no-argument constructor if the saloon name is not required. Ensure Main and any tests use the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for SealSaloon: the problem statement and UML specify a constructor SealSaloon(String) that takes the saloon name, but both the template's Main usage and the solution implement/use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This inconsistency can confuse students about the required API and whether to implement a String-taking constructor, causing extra cognitive load and potential failing tests or compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor, or (preferred) add the constructor public SealSaloon(String name) to SealSaloon.java (optionally keep the existing no-arg constructor for backwards compatibility) and update example usages in Main to call new SealSaloon("name"). This ensures the UML/text, template examples, and implementation match.
